title: Measure mode collapse
goal:
A GAN gives no density $p_g(x)$ (Section 6), so you compare samples. Write three functions to diagnose a generator on one-dimensional data.

- `histogram(samples, edges)` returns the probability mass in each bin as an array that sums to 1. Samples outside `[edges[0], edges[-1]]` are dropped before you normalize.
- `js_divergence(p, q)` returns the Jensen-Shannon divergence (natural log) of two histograms. Use the convention $0 \log 0 = 0$.
- `modes_covered(samples, modes, radius, min_frac)` returns how many of the centers in `modes` have at least `min_frac` of all samples within `radius` (distance strictly less than `radius`).

A generator that collapses onto one mode has a low value from `modes_covered` and a high `js_divergence` against the data, even when each sample it draws looks real.
hints: `np.histogram(samples, bins=edges)` returns counts. Divide by the counts' sum, not by `len(samples)`, so that dropped samples don't leave the mass below 1.
Reuse the divergence from exercise 1: `m = (p + q) / 2`, then two KL terms summed only where the first argument is positive.
Compute the fraction for each mode as `np.mean(np.abs(samples - c) < radius)`, and count the modes whose fraction is at least `min_frac`.
